en: Kindly keep my complaint number for reference.
tamil: என் புகார் எண்ணை குறிப்புக்காக வச்சுக்கோங்க.
context: Asking a helpdesk to note the case.
explain: 'Kindly' is formal Indian English for 'please'. 'For reference' means for later use.
usage: Use it in emails to customer care.
leelaQ: Do you note down complaint numbers?
answer: Yes, I save them on my phone.

en: Can you help me move this heavy box?
tamil: இந்த கனமான பெட்டியை நகர்த்த எனக்கு உதவி பண்ண முடியுமா?
context: Asking a neighbour for help.
explain: 'Help me' plus a base verb is simple. 'Heavy' describes the box.
usage: Ask this to a friend, neighbour or colleague for small physical help.
leelaQ: Who helps you at home with heavy work?
answer: My brother helps me with it.

en: Please switch off the fan before you leave.
tamil: போறதுக்கு முன்னாடி ஃபேனை அணைச்சிடுங்க.
context: Reminding a family member.
explain: A short polite instruction. 'Before you leave' sets the time.
usage: Use it at home or office to remind someone about a small duty.
leelaQ: What do you remind people to do before leaving?
answer: I remind them to lock the door.

en: Let me know if you need any help with this.
tamil: இதுல உங்களுக்கு எதாவது உதவி வேணும்னா சொல்லுங்க.
context: Offering support to a teammate.
explain: 'Let me know' invites the person to ask. 'If' makes it a gentle offer.
usage: A friendly line to offer help to a colleague without pushing.
leelaQ: How do you offer help to a busy friend?
answer: I tell them to call me if they need anything.

en: Could you speak a bit slowly? The line is not clear.
tamil: கொஞ்சம் மெதுவா பேச முடியுமா? லைன் தெளிவா இல்ல.
context: On a bad phone call.
explain: 'A bit' softens the request. The second sentence gives a reason.
usage: Use it on a phone call with poor signal or fast talkers.
leelaQ: What do you do when the signal is weak?
answer: I move near a window or call again.

en: Please do not close the ticket until it is solved.
tamil: இது தீருற வரைக்கும் டிக்கெட்டை க்ளோஸ் பண்ணாதீங்க.
context: Asking IT support to keep a case open.
explain: 'Do not' makes a polite negative instruction. 'Until' sets the limit.
usage: Use it with an IT or customer care team when cases get closed too soon.
leelaQ: Why is it bad to close a case too early?
answer: The problem may come back and no one will check.

en: Can I have a written confirmation of this refund?
tamil: இந்த ரீஃபண்டுக்கு எழுத்து மூலமா உறுதிப்படுத்தல் கிடைக்குமா?
context: Asking a store for proof in writing.
explain: 'Written confirmation' is proof. 'Can I have' is a common polite request.
usage: Say this when a shop promises money back and you want proof.
leelaQ: Why is a written proof useful?
answer: It protects me if there is a dispute later.

en: Please hold on, I will check it right now.
tamil: ஒரு நிமிஷம் இருங்க, இப்போவே பாக்கறேன்.
context: On a call with a customer.
explain: 'Hold on' means wait on the phone. 'Right now' shows you act at once.
usage: A common line on phone calls when you need a moment to look something up.
leelaQ: How do you ask a caller to wait?
answer: I say hold on please and check quickly.

en: Could you share your order number with me?
tamil: உங்க ஆர்டர் நம்பரை என்கிட்ட பகிர முடியுமா?
context: Support agent asking for details.
explain: 'Share with me' means give me. Support agents need this number first.
usage: Support agents ask this at the start of every complaint.
leelaQ: Do you save your order numbers?
answer: I keep the email so I can find them.

en: Please sit down, and I will take a look at it.
tamil: உட்காருங்க, நான் அதை பாக்கறேன்.
context: Welcoming an upset customer.
explain: A calm, polite offer. 'Take a look' means to check it.
usage: Shop or clinic staff say this to calm someone.
leelaQ: What makes a customer feel welcome?
answer: A smile and a quick reply.

en: Can you move your car? It is blocking our gate.
tamil: உங்க காரை நகர்த்த முடியுமா? அது எங்க கேட்டை அடைக்குது.
context: Asking a neighbour politely.
explain: State the problem after the request. 'Blocking' means stopping the way.
usage: Use it with a neighbour when someone parks in the wrong place.
leelaQ: How do you talk to a neighbour about a parking problem?
answer: I ask politely and explain why.

en: I cannot open the link you sent me.
tamil: நீங்க அனுப்பின லிங்கை என்னால திறக்க முடியல.
context: Telling a colleague a link fails.
explain: 'Cannot' shows you are unable. State what you tried for a faster answer.
usage: Say this in chat when a shared link is broken.
leelaQ: What do you do if a link does not work?
answer: I ask the person to send it again.

en: I do not understand why the fee is so high.
tamil: கட்டணம் ஏன் இவ்வளவு அதிகம்னு எனக்கு புரியல.
context: Questioning a bank charge.
explain: 'Do not understand why' is polite but clear. It asks for an explanation.
usage: Say this at a bank or office when a charge looks wrong.
leelaQ: Have you seen charges that you did not expect?
answer: Yes, my bank added a small fee.

en: Nobody has replied to my email for three days.
tamil: மூணு நாளா என் ஈமெயிலுக்கு யாரும் பதில் சொல்லல.
context: Complaining to a manager.
explain: 'Nobody' already makes a sentence negative. 'For three days' shows duration.
usage: Use it when you escalate an unanswered email.
leelaQ: How long do you wait for a reply?
answer: I wait two days and then I remind them.

en: The fan is not working, and it is too hot here.
tamil: ஃபேன் வேலை செய்யல, இங்க ரொம்ப சூடா இருக்கு.
context: Complaining in a hostel or guest house.
explain: Two facts joined by 'and'. 'Too hot' means more than is comfortable.
usage: Say this to the hostel or hotel staff about a room problem.
leelaQ: How do you stay cool in summer?
answer: I use a fan and drink cold water.

en: I did not receive any confirmation message.
tamil: எனக்கு எந்த உறுதிப்படுத்தல் மெசேஜும் வரல.
context: Reporting a missing SMS or email.
explain: 'Did not receive' with 'any' makes a strong negative. Common with bookings.
usage: Use it after booking tickets or paying a bill online.
leelaQ: What messages do you get after you pay?
answer: I get an SMS and an email.

en: Please do not worry, we will solve it today.
tamil: கவலைப்படாதீங்க, இன்னைக்கே நாங்க இதை தீர்த்து வைப்போம்.
context: Calming a worried customer.
explain: 'Do not worry' comforts people. Add a clear promise to make it real.
usage: Say this to a customer or a friend who is anxious.
leelaQ: What do you say to calm a worried person?
answer: I say do not worry and I offer help.

en: I have never had such a bad experience here.
tamil: இங்க இவ்வளவு மோசமான அனுபவம் எனக்கு எப்பவும் ஆனதில்ல.
context: Giving strong feedback to a restaurant.
explain: 'Never' with the present perfect speaks about your whole life up to now.
usage: Use it in a formal complaint or a review.
leelaQ: What was your best service experience?
answer: A hotel upgraded my room for free.

en: There is no hot water in the bathroom.
tamil: பாத்ரூம்ல வெந்நீர் வரல.
context: Telling hotel reception.
explain: 'There is no' states something is missing. Short and clear for staff.
usage: Say this at reception when a room facility is missing.
leelaQ: Do you prefer hot or cold water for a bath?
answer: I prefer hot water in the morning.

en: We could not finish the repair because the part was missing.
tamil: பார்ட் இல்லாததால எங்களால ரிப்பேரை முடிக்க முடியல.
context: A technician explaining a delay.
explain: 'Because' gives the reason. Explain the missing part so people do not blame you.
usage: Technicians use this when they must return another day.
leelaQ: Why do repairs sometimes take many days?
answer: Because some parts are not available quickly.

en: I am not able to attend the meeting due to a power cut.
tamil: கரண்ட் கட் காரணமா என்னால மீட்டிங்ல கலந்துக்க முடியாது.
context: Informing your team of an absence.
explain: 'Not able to' is a polite form of 'cannot'. 'Due to' gives a reason.
usage: Send this in a team chat when something stops you from joining.
leelaQ: What would you do if the power goes off during a call?
answer: I would join from my phone.

en: My card got blocked after the third wrong PIN.
tamil: மூணாவது தடவை PIN தப்பா போட்டதுக்கு அப்புறம் என் card block ஆயிடுச்சு.
context: Explaining a blocked card to a bank officer.
explain: 'Got blocked' shows something happened to the card, not by your choice.
usage: Say it at a bank counter or on a helpline when your card stops working.
leelaQ: What would you tell the bank about a blocked card?
answer: I would say my card got blocked after wrong PIN attempts.

en: Could you give me a discount for the trouble?
tamil: இந்த சிரமத்துக்கு ஒரு discount கொடுக்க முடியுமா?
context: Asking a shopkeeper for compensation after a problem.
explain: 'Could you' makes the request polite, even when you are unhappy.
usage: Use it politely in a shop or hotel after poor service.
leelaQ: What would you ask for after bad service?
answer: I would politely ask for a small discount.

en: Don't worry, I will fix it before you come back.
tamil: கவலைப்படாதீங்க, நீங்க திரும்ப வர்றதுக்குள்ள நான் இத சரி பண்ணிடுவேன்.
context: Reassuring a family member about a broken lamp.
explain: 'Will' shows a promise to solve the problem soon.
usage: Say it to family or a friend when you promise to repair something.
leelaQ: How do you calm someone when something breaks?
answer: I tell them not to worry and that I will fix it.

en: The seller never answered my calls about the return.
tamil: return பத்தி நான் பண்ண calls-க்கு seller எப்பவும் பதில் சொல்லல.
context: Complaining about an online seller to customer care.
explain: 'Never' makes the negative strong, showing a repeated problem.
usage: Use it when you complain to customer care about a seller who ignores you.
leelaQ: What would you say about a seller who ignores you?
answer: I would say the seller never answered my calls.
